excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: I know archive nodes store all transactions but do they also store the calldata within the transactions even if it's not used for contract calls?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: yes

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: The calldata is part of the transactions (and is needed for correctly computing the txhash, even if it is not used in the call), only the blob data will be deleted by archive nodes

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Even though calldata is not part of the state?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: yes

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Ok, thank you

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The transactions response should contain the type byte of blob transactions, just like for all other transacrions.

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: If that can't be inferred from the spec, we should clarify the spec

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: And full nodes store the first 128 blocks, do they also store every contract that has ever been deployed too? Because the contracts are part of the state? And only the archive nodes store all calldata since calldata is not part of the state?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Full nodes also store all calldata

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Full nodes store all transactions (and their calldata) as well as the state for the most recent 128 blocks. Archive nodes store all transactions as well as the state for all blocks. You can always recreate an archive node from a full node (and vice versa of course)

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Full nodes store all calldata of the first 128 blocks, and archive nodes store all calldata since Genesis right?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: No full nodes store ALL calldata

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Even beyond 128 blocks?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yes

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: But they don't store the associated transactions!?

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: How would that work

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: They store all associated transactions

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: They do not store the intermediate states

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Now I'm confused

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Full nodes store ALL transactions

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Then what about the 128 blocks?

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: What does that mean

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Then what's the difference to archive nodes and why are those 5 times as large

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: A block contains transactions, executing a block means you take the current state `s`, execute the transactions and end up with a state `s2`. Once you execute the block you don't need `s` anymore. Full nodes delete `s`, archive node store `s`

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: And both node types store all blocks, all transactions, and all calldata since Genesis and the only difference is that archive nodes store all states as well and full nodes only the current one?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: yes exactly

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Ohhh wow

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: And the state includes the code and storage for all contracts right?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: yes

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Omg thank you so much haha

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: I swear the documentation online doesn't convey it like that haha

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: The history is ~500GB, the state is ~80GB, the history of states is 15TB (or 800GB if you store them like erigon)

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Damn I would have thought the history is way larger

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: Because of all this calldata

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: So does that mean archive nodes make a copy of every contract's storage after EVERY SINGLE block even though most don't change and you end up with thousands of copies?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: yes, thats essentially what geth does (not for much longer), erigon only makes a copy of the storages that change
